question.problem: Given the hyperboloid of two sheets $(x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}-\frac{(z+5)^{2}}{16}=-1,$ find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}-\frac{(z+5)^{2}}{16} & =-1 \\ (x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+1 & =\frac{(z+5)^{2}}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(z+5)^{2}}{16} & =(x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+1 \\ (z+5)^{2} & =16((x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+1) \\ z+5 & =\pm 4\sqrt{(x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+1} \\ z & =-5\pm 4\sqrt{(x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

The square root is defined only for non-negative arguments. However, notice that for all $(x,y)\in {R}^{2},$ we have

$$
(x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+1\ge 0.
$$

Therefore, the domain of $z(x,y)$ is ${R}^{2}.$
